# Average of coarse and fine integrals [S1]

The claim '# Average of coarse and fine integrals [S1]' accurately reflects the content of Source [S1]. The source explicitly defines the total transient signal as the average of the coarse integral ($	au_c$) and the fine integral ($	au_f$) using the formula $	au(x', y', t) =  rac{	au_c(x', y', t) + 	au_f(x', y', t)}{2}$. The notes and passages confirm that $	au_c$ is estimated with coarse samples and $	au_f$ is estimated with fine samples from MCMC, and they are combined (averaged) to evaluate reconstruction quality.

- NeTF uses an MLP structure analogous to NeRF but with ReLU activations and simplified final layers [S1].

The claim states that NeTF uses an MLP structure analogous to NeRF but with ReLU activations and simplified final layers. Source [S1] explicitly confirms this in the caption for Fig. 7: 'we adopt an MLP structure analogous to the one used in NeRF. The key differences are (1) NeTF uses ReLU vs. NeRF uses sigmoid and (2) the last four layers in NeRF are simplified to one layer.' Additionally, Section 5.1 states: 'Analogous to NeRF [39], we construct a fully connected network... We use ReLU activations for all the layers.' Therefore, every fact in the claim is present in the evidence.
supported
- **Strengths:** Balances reconstruction quality and computational overhead; intrinsically differentiable; handles the 2D nature of hemispherical wavefronts unlike 1D ray sampling [S1].

The claim is fully supported by the evidence. 1. 'Balances reconstruction quality and computational overhead': The text states, 'Denser samples produce higher quality reconstruction. At the same time, they lead to a much higher computation overhead... we develop a coarse-to-fine sampling scheme' to address this. 2. 'Intrinsically differentiable': The text explicitly states, 'It is important to note that our hierarchical sampling is intrinsically differentiable'. 3. 'Handles the 2D nature of hemispherical wavefronts unlike 1D ray sampling': The text notes, 'NeTF calculates the integral along a ray, i.e., using 1D sampling, whereas NeTF on a hemisphere, i.e., using 2D sampling' and mentions that previous methods found resampling on the hemisphere intractable, implying NeTF handles it effectively.
supported
